reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses diffusion barrier failure temperatures for multi-component alloy films in Si/Cu stacks, not ZrN or Cr–Zr systems. It provides no specific support for the key premises regarding ZrN's properties, its effectiveness as a diffusion barrier in the proposed system, or its stability under the specified conditions.
premises: ZrN is chemically inert and has low atomic diffusivity, enabling it to act as a diffusion barrier.
An ultrathin (~50 nm) ZrN interlayer can suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion at 800–900 °C.
The ZrN interlayer will remain stable and effective under high-temperature steam and thermal cycling.
The ZrN interlayer will not degrade protective performance under normal subcritical water operation.
